title: In-app “Make it Live” publish help route and entry points

requirements.summary: Add an in-app help view explaining how to publish permanently when the Go Live/Publish button is not visible, including troubleshooting and fallback rebuild guidance.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can open a help view from within the app without relying on the external chat UI.

The help view includes step-by-step instructions to find the Go Live/Publish button (e.g., where it appears in the chat interface) and includes at least 3 troubleshooting tips (e.g., scroll, try another browser, disable extensions/ad blockers, zoom out).
The help view explains that drafts expire and that only publishing via the chat UI makes the deployment permanent.
The help view includes a section that explains the user’s fallback action requested (“create a new one”) as: rebuilding a new draft version, and what to expect (draft still expires until published).

file_operations.description: Create the “Make it Live” help page content (step-by-step where to find Go Live/Publish in the external chat UI; at least 3 troubleshooting tips; explanation that drafts expire and only external publish makes it permanent; fallback section describing rebuilding a new draft and what to expect). Include clear headings and concise, scannable lists; do not claim any in-app publishing capability; include a clear return action (back + home).

requirements.summary: Add entry points to the “Make it Live” help surface from the Landing Page and from the authenticated dashboard header area.
acceptanceCriteria: Landing Page includes a visible, accessible link/button labeled in English (e.g., “Make this app live”).
Dashboard view includes a visible, accessible entry point to the same help content for logged-in users.
Clicking either entry point opens the same help content (either a route or a modal) and does not break existing navigation.

file_operations.description: Add a visible, accessible CTA link/button on the Landing Page labeled in English (e.g., “Make this app live”) that navigates to the /publish-help route (same help content). Ensure it fits existing hero layout and does not interfere with current auth/shared-hub flows.

Add a dashboard-header entry point by inserting a new item in the existing user dropdown menu (authenticated/known-user context) that navigates to /publish-help (same help content). Ensure accessible label and that existing menu actions (share/logout) continue to work.

requirements.summary: Register a dedicated /publish-help route in the TanStack Router tree and provide a clear way to return.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to /publish-help renders the help content.
The route is registered in the router configuration and does not affect existing routes.
The help page provides a clear way to return to the previous page or the home page.

file_operations.description: Wire the new /publish-help route into the TanStack Router route tree by importing the new PublishHelpPage component, creating the route, and adding it to rootRoute children. Keep existing routes unchanged.

Ensure the page includes explicit navigation controls (e.g., “Back” and “Go to Home”) that work even when a user lands directly on /publish-help, satisfying the return-path requirement without altering other routes.
